runtimeRepairFindings.scenario: Shutdown aborts production publisher while a native WHATWG Response stream is awaiting a read and its cooperative async cancel() needs additional time to complete.
runtimeRepairFindings.observed: Publisher bounded() races abort without joining its operation, and readJson discards reader.cancel() promises. Runtime joins publisher.publish(), but that promise already settled while body cleanup continues. Reproduction returned from runtime.shutdown() with cleanupStarted=true and cleanupFinished=false; cleanup finished only after a gate was released after shutdown. The runtime persisted uncertain, preserving conservative send handling.
runtimeRepairFindings.expected: Production publisher must join its active operation and response cancellation cleanup before its publish promise settles, allowing runtime.shutdown() to drain all publisher work before shared resource closure. Keep finite native transport deadlines and conservative send outcomes.

runtimeRepairFindings.scenario: Call const starting = runtime.start(); const stopping = runtime.shutdown(); await starting; await stopping in one synchronous turn, then allow timers to run.
runtimeRepairFindings.observed: start() yields at await stopping when stopping is still null. shutdown() then aborts the lifetime, but the earlier start resumes and replaces that aborted controller with a fresh one, sets running=true and schedules the loop. With tickIntervalMs=10, the reproduction logged reads=0 when shutdown returned and reads=4 fifty milliseconds later. A timer and database work survive the later shutdown request.
runtimeRepairFindings.expected: Lifecycle operations must respect invocation order: a later shutdown cancels an earlier not-yet-started start; after that shutdown resolves no timers or reads may run unless a subsequent start was requested. Preserve the existing supported shutdown-then-start restart case.

runtimeRepairFindings.scenario: Production publisher receives confirmed POST HTTP 403 but body.cancel() requires async cleanup. Runtime send deadline fires during that cleanup. Publisher then drains and returns destination-unavailable.
runtimeRepairFindings.observed: Runtime bounded() waits for pending in finally but discards its result because the abort promise already won. send() handles the thrown timeout as uncertain whenever invoked=true. Independent reproduction captures publisherResult={outcome:destination-unavailable} but finishSend receives {outcome:uncertain}. Destination is not paused; publication is instead held as an uncertain tombstone. The same result-discard path affects explicit rejected/retryAt outcomes, including confirmed 429 and safe preflight rejection.
runtimeRepairFindings.expected: After draining a publisher operation, preserve its explicit NewsPublishResult even if cancellation started first. A typed confirmed result establishes safe rejection/destination failure or acceptance. Only unresolved/throwing publisher outcomes after invocation should become uncertain. Preserve source timeout classification separately if adjusting shared bounded helper.

acceptanceScenarios.evidence: Both destinations configured in one guild, store/runtime fully reopened, new eligible continuous item delivered to continuous destination and fresh daily edition to daily destination. Production REST validation/rendering/publisher used. Later independent guild gets only its own messages/status; actual main/Gateway connection is covered by application.test.ts.

Second continuous guild activated after collection takes the fresh snapshot baseline, skips old items and shares subsequent collection. Eight daily activation boundary/cache combinations pass; cached pre-window state is explicitly synthetic. First/late primary/fallback keys are asserted. A joining guild cannot reset an already completed missing primary. Sent and uncertain daily tombstones survive disable/new channel+role/restart.

Successful primary gives one edition per guild and no fallback request. Stale primary then fresh fallback yields one. Stale both yields none and exactly four bounded fixture HTTP requests (two listings, two candidates). Existing runtime tests also cover empty result/304 listing revalidation.

Production publisher confirmed 429 keeps one stored publication/nonce across restart; fallback is never scraped. At 22:00 pending work expires and a recovered next-morning publisher gets no POST. Production lost-response outcome is held uncertain, never automatically retried. Runtime suite proves completion/admission deadline races and failed receipt persistence.

A claimed pre-send publication is fenced after channel+role replacement; only the new configuration is rendered. Disable erases routing and cancels claimed work; same-day never-sent re-enable may replan. A POST already issued before disable finishes and retains its sent tombstone, documenting the unavoidable admitted-request race. Permission-loss pauses only the affected guild; explicit reconfiguration revalidates/resumes.

Repeated ID/minor correction produces no new post; an older unimportant story promoted within 24 hours sends once. A ten-story synthetic burst through actual Mongo/runtime yields six sends, omits four after the exact two-hour horizon, and never bursts after restart. Separate captured-time replay covers 50 actual source IDs/timestamps across five dates with 301 simulated shared polls, 50 sends/guild, zero simulated expiries, 29.57-minute maximum publication delay and 20-minute maximum queue delay. Retain the 20-minute/two-hour policy on this limited evidence; no claim of historical delivery delay/loss or complete daily volume.

Real command/adapter/Mongo/publisher/restart journeys assert 20:00 local primary and durable date identity for January (CET), July (CEST), March 29 spring transition and October 25 autumn transition. policy.test.ts separately covers local/UTC midnight and all primary/fallback/deadline boundaries, plus same-local-date publication freshness. News uses Europe/Bratislava independently of the AI timezone.
